podcast.title: Dean Torrance's Army Enlistment
podcast.body: Dean Torrance, originally part of The Debarrens, enlisted in the army reserves for six months of basic training to avoid a longer draft. While in basic training, he heard "Jenny Lee" on the radio, credited to Jan and Arnie, and was convinced he could hear his own voice, leading him to regret his military choice. "And Dean Torrance was off in the army, regretting his choices."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Discovery by Joe Lubin
podcast.body: After Jan Berry and Arnie Ginsburg re-recorded "Jenny Lee," Jan took an acetate copy to a friend's party. Joe Lubin, Vice President of Arwin Records (owned by Marty Melcher, Doris Day's husband), happened to hear it from another room while Jan was having the acetate cut. Lubin was impressed and promised to make Jan and Arnie "bigger than the Elderly Brothers," eventually overdubbing instruments and releasing the track. "Joe Lubin overdubbed extra instruments on the track and released it."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
